analysis: The PR changes one documentation sentence in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 296-297, patch hunk @@ -293,7 +293,8 @@). It says the switch command scans local models in the daemon's resolved config `model_cache_directory`. Only base text from line 822 onward was supplied. That text is unchanged context, so the changed `switch` section itself was not visible and was not directly examined. The patch excerpt was the only evidence for the change. The change is documentation-only: no code, authentication, attestation, encryption, billing or coordinator logic is touched. I found no regression against the threat model. Relevant context: T-012 and A-004 cover model-weight tampering in the cache directory, and T-041 covers cache-storage trust. The sentence documents that model discovery follows the daemon's configured cache path. Documentation does not change the controls on weight integrity. Those controls still depend on the model-hash and load-time verification described elsewhere. The base-text context also references the operator-selected cache and the `models location` check, and it correctly says discovery is not weight-integrity verification. I identified no unverified contract that needs a finding. The implementation in the Swift `switch` command (that it actually scans the daemon's configured directory and validates artifacts) was not supplied. That would be a code-review question for another pass, not a documentation security issue.
